about.tool: A broad-edged pen held at a low angle, about 25° on this exemplar (the old books go as flat as 10-20°), so stems are heavy, level strokes about half as thick, and the thinnest point of a round letter is at its upper left.
about.proportions: About 4 nib widths tall; round and wide: O 1.2 times as wide as tall, M and W 1.75. d, h, k, l and F's arm rise about a quarter of the height; j, g, p, y fall about a quarter, and q's tail and x a little.
about.features: Round unicase letters: the a-shaped A, the round d whose ascender hooks back over the bowl, the h-shaped H, the three-stroke m-shaped M, the U of a flagged bar, a bow and a stem; stems start with a flag and the heavy diagonals of A, V, W, X, Y with a hook. Simplified here: the flags are drawn as the pen sliding along its edge, and the pen angle stays fixed (the sheet turns it steeper for N's thin right stem and the thin leg of A, which come out heavier here).
about.history: The book hand of the late Roman and early Christian world, 4th to 8th centuries, grown from Roman capitals written quickly with a broad pen; Insular scribes in Ireland and Britain carried it on, and its cousin Half-Uncial is the hand of the Book of Kells. The figures are a modern addition.
